article.description:
When Tari Phillips is matched against 7-foot-2 Utah center Margo Dydek, the New York Liberty center knows
how to score.
article.headline: New York rallies from 11-point deficit to win
article.linkText: Phillips goes over Dydek for 22 as New York tops Utah
article.story:
SALT LAKE CITY (AP) -- When Tari Phillips is matched against 7-foot-2 Utah center Margo Dydek, the New York Liberty center knows how to score. ``Just concentrate on making some outside shots. Make her step out away from the basket and mix it up,'' Phillips said after scoring 22 points in New York's 71-68 victory over the Utah Starzz on Tuesday. Crystal Robinson added 17 points and New York rallied from an 11-point deficit. Teresa Weatherspoon put the Liberty (6-2) ahead 69-68 when she split the lane for an uncontested layup with 20.9 seconds remaining. ``We all played well. We focused in the end and made a run,'' Phillips said. Adrienne Goodson, who scored 18 points for Utah, was called for an offensive foul on the ensuing possession. Robinson and Vickie Johnson each made one free throw in the final 9.5 seconds to seal the victory. Marie Ferdinand scored 18 points for Utah (4-3), but missed three of four free throws in the final minute. The Starzz committed 10 of their 20 turnovers in the last 10½ minutes. ``We had our chances to blow them out,'' Ferdinand said. ``We had a good lead midway through the second half. We let them turn the game away by turning the ball over and not handling the press.'' Down 69-68, the Starzz blew a chance for the lead with 4.1 seconds to go when Natalie Williams was wide open under the basket but couldn't handle a quick pass from Ferdinand. ``I think fatigue caught up with us,'' said Utah coach Candi Harvey, whose team played its third game in four days. Dydek, back in Utah's starting lineup after two games as a reserve, scored 12 points and tied a career high with 16 rebounds. The Starzz led 50-39 on Ferdinand's layup with 12 minutes remaining. Becky Hammon hit two long jumpers and New York answered with a 13-0 run, taking a 52-50 lead on a layup by former Utah point guard Korie Hlede. Game notes
New York posted the 100th victory in franchise history, becoming the third WNBA team to reach that milestone. ... Six of Utah's seven games have been decided by five points or less. They are 4-2 in those games. ... Utah forward Kate Starbird went scoreless in four minutes after coming off the injured list. Rookie forward Danielle Crockrom went on the list with a bruised right shin.
